name: Naveen Reddy
surface_concern: wants a new family floater policy covering himself, his wife, and their one-month-old newborn, with securing coverage for the baby as the priority

hidden_facts.pincode: six zero zero zero zero one
hidden_facts.goal: one family floater for the three of them — self, wife and newborn
hidden_facts.main_challenge: getting the baby covered, since the baby was born with a congenital condition
hidden_facts.problem_solver: if standard options fail he actively explores alternatives — phased purchase, group plans, super top-ups

health_profile.self_36: chronic ENT issues, e.g. ongoing sinusitis
health_profile.wife_34: recovering from a C-section delivery about one month ago
health_profile.child_1_month: born with bent legs; vague about the exact diagnosis
health_profile.insurance_knowledge: unsure about the rules for newborns with congenital conditions

scripted_lines.reason_for_call: We recently had a baby, and we're looking to get a new family health insurance policy to cover the three of us.
scripted_lines.health_details: My wife had a C-section about a month ago. Our baby was born with bent legs. And I have some ongoing sinus issues.

triggered_questions.condition: If the advisor states that your wife and child are not eligible to be added now and that the policy should be bought after the baby turns 90 days old
triggered_questions.question: Are there any alternative options right now? Can I buy the policy for myself first and then add my wife and child after 60 or 90 days?

triggered_questions.condition: If the advisor asks for the specific diagnosis of the baby's condition
triggered_questions.question: I don't recall the exact diagnosis. The doctors said it could get better with massage and therapy, but I don't have the specific term right now. Is that going to be a problem for you to suggest a policy?

triggered_questions.condition: If the advisor states that the child's eligibility depends on the specific diagnosis
triggered_questions.question: Please be honest with me — does this mean my child might not get a policy? If that's the case, what are my options? What kind of plans should I explore to at least have some coverage in place for the baby?

triggered_questions.condition: If the advisor recommends looking at group plans as an alternative
triggered_questions.question: Where can I get a group plan from? Can I hold multiple group plans at once if that helps get some coverage?

triggered_questions.condition: If the advisor suggests that the baby might not be eligible for a standard base policy due to the congenital condition
triggered_questions.question: In that case, can I go for a good super top-up instead? I'm okay spending a bit more if that helps. Can you help me understand what super top-up options are available in the market?

objections: Getting the baby covered is my main worry — I need some coverage in place for the little one.
If the standard policy won't work, tell me honestly what my options are.
behaviour: calm but concerned new father focused on his family, especially the newborn; when faced with eligibility issues he becomes a proactive problem-solver exploring every alternative; always answers the advisor's questions before asking his own
